title: What happens to the mean and median after small weight changes?
description: A group has a mean weight of sixty five point three kilograms and a median of sixty seven. One person loses two kilograms and two persons gain one each. The total weight does not change, so the mean stays, but the median depends on who changed.
teaching_notes: One idea: the mean follows the total, and the changes cancel to zero, while the median depends on where the changed persons sit in the sorted list. Watch for students who say the median also stays because the total stays.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 8)
video_script.why: A child who has used the total to find a missing value now sees that changes which cancel leave the mean fixed while the median can still move.
video_script.substitution: the book's group with mean weight 65.3 kg and median 67 kg; for the check, an example group of ten persons with total 653 kg
video_script.anchor: a group of people on a weighing scale with the mean 65.3 kg and the median 67 kg marked
video_script.payoff_line: The mean is unchanged, and nothing can be said about the median

final_answer.value: mean unchanged; median cannot be told
final_answer.spoken: the mean is unchanged, and nothing can be said about the median

never_show: a statement that the median stays at 67 kg or moves, marked as right
maths_rules: the number of people stays the same, so mean = total ÷ count stays 65.3 kg
the median depends on which three persons changed and where they sit in the sorted list, which is not given, so nothing can be said
check: an example group of ten persons with total 653 kg has mean 65.3 kg; after the changes the total is 653 − 2 + 1 + 1 = 653 and 653 ÷ 10 = 65.3
video_script.design: One group of people on a weighing scale all video. The three changes appear as small arrows and cancel on a running total, while the sorted line of weights stays hidden for the median.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the mean and the median.
<bookmark mark='group'/>A group of people has a mean weight of sixty five point three kilograms. The median weight is sixty seven kilograms.
<bookmark mark='change'/>This month one person loses two kilograms. Two other persons gain one kilogram each.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What can we say about the change in the mean and the median?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.median: a sorted line of weights appears with the middle marked

narration: <bookmark mark='mean'/>The mean is the total weight shared by the number of people.
<bookmark mark='median'/>The median is the weight in the middle of the sorted list.

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a mean of sixty five point three kilograms and a median of sixty seven kilograms. One person loses two kilograms, and two persons gain one kilogram each.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to say what happens to the mean. Then say what happens to the median.

narration: <bookmark mark='lose'/>Step one, find the change in the total weight. The changes are minus two, plus one and plus one.
<bookmark mark='gain'/>Add them up. Minus two plus one plus one is zero.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The total weight of the group does not change.

marks.mean: the same total divided by the same count gives 65.3 kg

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, the number of people stays the same. Nobody joins and nobody leaves.
<bookmark mark='mean'/>The same total shared by the same count gives the same mean, sixty five point three kilograms.

beats.on_screen: median: depends on who the three persons are and where they sit in the sorted list; not given

narration: <bookmark mark='who'/>Step three, the median depends on who the three persons are. We do not know where they sit in the sorted list.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>A person near the middle can move the middle value.
<bookmark mark='far'/>A person far from the middle may leave it where it is.
<bookmark mark='cant'/>The information is not enough to say what happens to the median.

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Check the mean with a group of ten persons. Their total weight is six hundred and fifty three kilograms.
<bookmark mark='before'/>Divided by ten, that gives sixty five point three.
<bookmark mark='after'/>After the changes, the total is six hundred and fifty three minus two plus one plus one. That is six hundred and fifty three again.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Divided by ten, the mean is still sixty five point three.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Mean is unchanged; nothing can be said about the median
